To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glycogen, but no other energy store, limits survival of side-bloched lizards over winter, and that the amount of glycogen stored in lizards is not influenced by winter temperatures.

(1) Glycogen, not water loss, limits survival of side-bloched lizards overwintering under laboratory conditions; (2) Glycogen is a better predictor of winter survival than abdominal fat or tail mass; (3) The relationship between glycogen and survival is linear and not a threshold response; (4) Glycogen levels are not correlated with mass loss; (5) The relationship between water content and survival is non-linear and not a threshold effect.
